RESEARCH COMPLETED — notes.md carries a final RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:40 ET that supersedes an earlier one at 06:36, so nothing here is a truncation artifact. Four candidates were captured in five writes (GS twice; the later 1.5% version governs, per the last-entry-wins rule).

WHY ONLY FOUR IDEAS, AS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN APOLOGY. Levels were set on 13 instruments with a compliant stop and a target at or below the instrument's own 120-day high. Five cleared the 2.0 swing floor (GS 2.09, STLD 2.12, UNH 2.26, BAC 2.26, MS 2.10); BAC was cut on the correlation cap as the same trade as GS and MS. Failed outright: WFC 1.47, NUE 1.43, FCX 1.66, ETH-long 1.64, SOL 1.37, BTC 0.90, ADA 0.65. CLF reached 2.01 only with its stop sitting exactly on the floor, so it is on the watchlist rather than in the report. The pattern is the finding: everything that cleared is 16-23% below its 120-day high with a dated earnings catalyst, and everything that failed is either a leader with no room left (FCX -8.2%, WFC -9.2%, NUE -10.6%) or a crypto asset whose ATR is too wide.

RATIOS CLUSTER JUST ABOVE THE FLOOR AND THAT DESERVES SAYING. All four recomputed ratios land between 2.09 and 2.24 against a 2.0 swing floor, which is the signature of targets fitted to clear the bar. Two things argue it is not that here, and a reader should weigh both. First, the floor was not cleared from the stop side: recomputed stop distances are 2.52 ATR (GS), 2.50 (STLD), 2.54 (UNH) and 2.75 (MS), all above the 2.0 swing-stock floor and at or above the 2.5 comfortable level, and every target sits 5.27-5.88 ATR out, inside the 6.0 guide. Second, every target is at or below the instrument's own 120-day high and every level traces to a fetched price (a prior session high, a moving average, a 120-day extreme) rather than to a round number. The ideas that would have needed tuning are in the rejection blocks instead. Every figure above was recomputed in synthesis from the final entry, stop and target against freshly fetched ATR14 — not carried from the notes.

ALL FOUR ARE ONE STYLE, WHICH THE CORRELATION CAP CANNOT SEE. Four sectors (capital-markets banks twice, steel, managed care) but one methodology: buy a capitulated large cap into its own earnings print, entry above the market, confirmation required. If post-capitulation mean reversion does not work this month, all four fail together regardless of sector. The config counts drivers, not styles, so this is flagged by hand.

GS AND MS ARE ONE BET, NOT TWO. Both are capital-markets banks hit by the same OpenAI-IPO-deferral story and the same rate fear. They are sized at 1.5% each for that reason: treat the pair as a single 3.0% position and do not size them independently. Total capital at risk across the four is 8.0%, so the honest count is three independent bets.

SEPTEMBER CPI IS A SHARED SINGLE POINT OF FAILURE FOR THREE OF THE FOUR. CPI prints Tue 2026-10-14 08:30 ET. GS and UNH report 10-13 before the open and their entries trigger on that day's reaction, so both are one day old when CPI lands; MS reports on CPI morning itself. The driver behind all three drawdowns IS the rate path — the bank complex sold off specifically on fear of additional Fed hikes with TLT within 2% of its 120-day low — so a hot CPI re-fires the exact cause of the setups while the positions are at their most fragile. EXPLICIT INSTRUCTION: do not add size to any of them before 10-14 08:30 ET, and treat a simultaneous GS and UNH trigger on 10-13 as one position's worth of risk. STLD is the diversifier only by timing — its 10-19 print lands after CPI has resolved.

EVERY ENTRY SITS ABOVE FRIDAY'S CLOSE AND THREE OF FOUR CARRY wait: true. A likely and correct outcome is that some never trigger. This is a deliberate correction, not a quirk. The research phase priced all 13 priceable awaiting-entry ideas against Friday's close and found that ELEVEN OF THIRTEEN called the direction correctly and earned nothing, because every long was pitched below the market (6 for 6) and every short above it (5 for 5), so a correct call that simply moved never filled. VST is +22.3% past its entry, OXY +11.3%, FCX +8.1%, MU +7.2%; ITB -5.6% past, GLD -5.5%, AAL -4.4%. The report has been selecting against its own correct calls. The cost of the fix is real and stated: you pay up, the stop sits further away in price terms, and a trigger can fill and immediately reverse.

CONVICTION WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE EVIDENCE, NOT CARRIED. SOURCES THAT FAILED, AND WHAT EACH COST. (1) market_data.py macro hung twice and never returned, killed at 180s and 400s. No rates, VIX, DXY or FRED data at all — the regime read was rebuilt from ETF proxies, and THERE IS NO VIX FIGURE IN THIS RUN; the market_context levels for vix, us10y and dxy are null rather than estimated. (2) market_data.py events is structurally broken for discovery — it pulls only the first 200 open Kalshi markets and filters client-side, and all 200 returned belonged to a single movie series, so every search returns 0 results. Worked around via series_ticker, but then every price field (yes_bid, yes_ask, last_price, volume, open_interest) returned null on both the list and per-ticker endpoints. Event contracts were therefore impossible: universe.md requires a stated disagreement against the market's implied probability, and that number could not be fetched. The two event contracts already in awaiting-entry (KXFEDDECISION-26OCT-H25 @28, KXCPIYOY-26SEP-T3.5 @18) also could not be re-marked. (3) market_data.py implied returned HTTP 401 from yahoo-options, so THE OPTIONS-IMPLIED-MOVE CHECK COULD NOT BE RUN ON ANY IDEA TODAY — do not read any published target as having been tested against what the options market prices. (4) market_data.py short returned a ReadTimeout from api.nasdaq.com, so there is no short-interest or days-to-cover data for any name. (5) CoinGecko /market_chart 429'd on the third coin; crypto OHLC came from Kraken instead, and CoinGecko's free ohlc endpoint returns 4-day bars at days=90, which would have understated every crypto stop had it been used. (6) A generic 'week ahead' WebSearch returned 2013-2016 results and was useless; targeted searches worked.

TWO DATA CAVEATS WORTH THE READER'S TIME. The quote helper returned an identical change_pct of 0.4936% for both QQQ and IWM, almost certainly an artifact — only their price levels are relied on, which reconcile with the history series. And STLD's 120-day low refetched in synthesis reads 211.13 against the 219.10 recorded during research; the window has rolled. POSITION MANAGEMENT IS ON THE WATCHLIST, NOT IN THE RECOMMENDATIONS, AND FOR A MECHANICAL REASON. All 15 open positions were reviewed one by one: 8 hold as-is, 4 hold on notice (CCJ, LCII, BCC, KHC), 1 unchanged (DAL), and 2 close instructions. Real directional exposure is 11, not 15, because two 'positions' are boxed pairs — the book holds LULU buy @115 and LULU sell @100.61 simultaneously, and the identical shape in NKE. In both pairs the short is the leg that is working and the long is the leg with no stop and no invalidation. The decision is to close the long legs and keep the shorts, and it could not be published as a candidate row: the live shorts are stored as direction 'sell' rather than 'sell_short', so a sell candidate on either name would be merged into the live short as an amendment and would overwrite its stop and target. There is no direction value that expresses 'exit a long' without colliding. Likewise the trailing stops on DINO (+12.8%) and CEG (+9.6%) are instructions rather than amendments, because check_stop_distance measures from entry.ideal and a filled position's entry may never change — a DINO stop at 105 is 0.56 ATR from the 107.50 entry and fails outright, and CEG's existing 250 stop is already only 1.51 ATR from its 272 entry because ATR has expanded to 14.52. Publishing those would have produced ideas engineered to be demoted. All six management items are written up as watchlist rows so they reach the reader.

RED TEAM (phase 2c, separate pass, did not write the above). CUT TWO OF FOUR, DOWNGRADED BOTH SURVIVORS. Two remain: MS rank 1 and STLD rank 2, both at conviction 3.

CUT UNH (was rank 1, conviction 4, 2.5%) — the stop is inside the range, not under it. The idea disclosed this as its weak point; a fresh 120-bar fetch shows it is worse than disclosed. The 367.00 stop was traded through twice in the eight sessions before the entry has ever printed (365.72 on 09-30, 362.60 on 10-01), with 368.05 and 368.50 either side. Disclosure is not a fix. The honest stop below 362.60 gives 1.80 R:R against a 2.0 floor, so the idea never cleared it, and the only rescue is a 445.50 target at 6.32 ATR — past the 6.0 guide every other idea here respected. stop_distance passing at 2.54 ATR is the ATR proxy failing on a compressed range.

CUT GS (was rank 4, conviction 3, 1.5%) — thesis mechanism falsified by news the run missed, plus a contradicting evidence leg, plus concentration. Its positioning evidence argues against the trade in its own words (flat revisions, 46.9% bullish with a strong-sell, underperforms SPY on every window), which is not a confirmation. More decisively: the 'deferral not impairment' mechanism rests on the OpenAI IPO delay, which broke 2026-06-26 — not in the drawdown it is used to explain — and on 2026-10-08, the day before this report's reference close, the FT reported OpenAI now tells investors annualised revenue is approaching $50bn against roughly $70bn previously indicated. That reprices the fee pool rather than postponing it. And the report itself concedes GS and MS are one bet with MS the stronger, while notes.md recorded a decision to publish only ONE bank idea because XLF already sits in awaiting-entry on the same driver.

DOWNGRADED MS 4 to 3 and STLD 4 to 3. MS: the OpenAI leg of its thesis is weakened by the same 10-08 revenue report, now written into its thesis and key_risk instead of omitted, and its positioning leg is sell-side revision drift that the idea's own counter_argument calls a thin reed. Size held at 1.5% even though its paired half was cut, because CPI prints alongside its earnings and XLF is still live on the same driver. STLD: its own revision signal is +1.7pp and its four surprises average about +2% with one miss, which is near noise, and the pricing case is a read-across from Cleveland-Cliffs; it is also the only surviving idea that holds through its own print.

SOURCE INTEGRITY, THREE FINDINGS. (1) The single hard validation failure on all four ideas was the same citation: api.nasdaq.com/api/quote/<SYM>/historical 404s, with or without query params, because it is a machine endpoint that rejects HEAD. The data behind it is real — it is what market_data.py fetches — so this was a bad citation, not a bad number, and the surviving ideas now cite www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/<sym>/historical, which resolves 200 and a reader can actually open. Had this been left, phase 2d would have demoted all four ideas over a URL format. (2) STLD's thesis attributed the Wells Fargo upgrade to Overweight, the GLJ raise and the JPMorgan raise to the 247wallst article, which contains none of them — it was fetched and checked, and confirms only the ASP figures ($1,124/net ton Q2 vs $1,048 Q1) and the CLF move. The analyst actions are nonetheless REAL and were independently verified: Wells Fargo to Overweight from Equal Weight on 2026-10-06, $12 to $14, Timna Tanners, citing steel pricing power and near-pandemic lead times. A correct claim on the wrong URL, so the fix is the citation, not the idea. (3) The news URLs were all live (CNBC, moomoo, 247wallst all 200); none was hallucinated.

ONE VALIDATOR ARTIFACT TO IGNORE, AND ONE STALE NUMBER FIXED. Every idea carries earnings_date: warn, 'claims an earnings catalyst but X is not on the fetched calendar'. That warning is wrong — a fresh `market_data.py earnings --days 14` returns all four at the exact dates and estimates claimed (UNH 10-13 bmo 4.1893, MS 10-14 bmo 3.1669, STLD 10-19 amc 5.4904, GS 10-13 bmo 15.0539), and the cause is a bug in the validator rather than anything wrong with the ideas. validate_report.py calls market_data.earnings(45); finnhub caps that response at exactly 1500 rows and returns the FAR end of the window, so a 45-day request comes back covering only 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-24 and contains no October at all. The same call at 14 days returns all four names correctly. The effect is that check_earnings_date warns on every idea whose earnings are inside the next few weeks — precisely the case it exists to check — so the flag is uninformative here and the dated_catalyst leg should not be discounted on the strength of it. Worth fixing in the validator, with a test; left alone by this phase, which does not change code. Separately, STLD's technical evidence carried a 120-day low of 219.10, which the refetch confirms is the 10-01 session low; the true 120-day low is 211.13, and the evidence now says so. All of MS's and STLD's entry and stop levels were re-verified bar by bar against a fresh 120-day fetch and are exact: MS 193.14 is the 10-06 high and its 181.90 stop sits below the 182.47 120-day low; STLD 245.185 is the 10-05 high.

WHAT THE CUTS DID TO CONCENTRATION, WHICH WAS THE POINT. The run flagged by hand that all four ideas were one methodology and that three of four shared September CPI as a single point of failure. Cutting UNH and GS leaves one name that reports on CPI morning and clears both events in one trigger, and one that reports on 10-19 after CPI has resolved — different sectors, different dates, and capital at risk down from 8.0% to 4.0%. Two conviction-3 ideas is a thinner report than four conviction-4 ideas and a more honest one.

recommendations.thesis: Morgan Stanley has beaten consensus in four consecutive quarters — by 14.11%, 10.92%, 6.78% and 29.27% — and sell-side positioning is the one thing in the bank complex actually improving, with bullish share up 4.4 points to 60.6% while BAC deteriorated 3.5 points and GS sat flat at 46.9%. The stock is nonetheless 18.18% below its 120-day high of 232.25, because the whole group has been marked down on rate fear and because the OpenAI IPO delay pushed equity-capital-markets fees into 2027. The red team has downgraded that second leg rather than removed it: the delay is real and MS is an adviser, but it broke on 2026-06-26, not in the drawdown this thesis explains, and on 2026-10-08 the FT reported OpenAI now tells investors annualised revenue is approaching $50bn against roughly $70bn previously indicated — so the fee pool is partly repriced, not purely deferred. What survives is the narrower claim: ECM is the business line most sensitive to a calendar, and a slipped calendar is recoverable in a way a credit loss is not. Price has already stopped making lows: the 120-day low of 182.47 printed 2026-10-01 and has been followed by a sequence of higher lows at 185.22, 186.15 and 187.05. The trade is that Q3 lands on the same morning the macro question is answered, and a fifth straight beat into a cleared CPI is what takes the stock back through the 195.99 20-day toward the 207.33 50-day.
recommendations.key_risk: OPENAI IS NOT A CLEAN DEFERRAL ANY MORE, and that is the red team's addition to this idea. On 2026-10-08 the FT reported OpenAI's annualised revenue is approaching $50bn against the roughly $70bn previously indicated, and the IPO is pushed to early 2027. If the eventual listing is smaller or later than the pipeline assumes, the ECM fee line is repriced rather than merely postponed, and the mean-reversion mechanism this thesis names is weaker than the word 'deferral' implies. A hot September CPI on the morning of 2026-10-14 re-fires exactly the driver that caused this drawdown, and because it prints alongside the earnings the two cannot be separated — a good quarter can be entirely overwhelmed by the macro number, and the 193.14 trigger would simply never fire. That is the single largest risk to the trade and it is unhedgeable, which is why the 1.5% size is retained even though the GS half of the pair has been cut. Note the correlation warning in the original idea is now partly spent: the red team cut GS, so this is no longer half of a 3% paired position. But XLF BUY still sits in awaiting-entry on this same bank-earnings driver, so size this against that exposure rather than as a standalone. There is also no insider confirmation at all: zero open-market purchases against 17 sales in six months, and the positioning leg is sell-side revision drift, which this idea's own counter_argument correctly calls a thin reed.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that four straight beats have already happened and the stock is still 18% off its high, which says the market is not pricing MS off its earnings at all — it is pricing the rate path and the deal calendar, neither of which a Q3 beat settles. On that reading the improving sell-side revision trend is just analysts marking to a print they can forecast while the thing that actually matters is unforecastable. The second objection is mine against myself: I chose MS over BAC on revision direction, but BAC also beat four of four and has the tidier chart target, and the honest answer is that the revision screen is a thin reed to pick between two good setups. The entry condition is the partial answer to both — requiring a reclaim of 193.14 after both events means the trade only pays up once the market has resolved the questions the thesis cannot.

recommendations.thesis: Steel equities are in an upgrade cycle while the group still trades below its summer levels, and Steel Dynamics is the profitable way to own it. Analyst revisions have turned measurably positive across the complex — Wells Fargo moved Cleveland-Cliffs to Overweight from Equal Weight on 2026-10-06, target $12 to $14, analyst Timna Tanners, explicitly citing steel pricing power and hot-rolled-coil lead times near pandemic-era levels, with target raises from GLJ and JPMorgan alongside (red team: these actions were verified against the Investing.com report of the upgrade, because the 247wallst article originally cited for them does not contain them) — and realised pricing is confirming it, with CLF's average selling price at 1,124 dollars per net ton in Q2 against 1,048 in Q1. STLD itself has beaten consensus in three of its last four quarters and earns 3.81 a share against CLF's four straight losses, so the same pricing leverage arrives on an income statement that is already in profit. The chart has stopped breaking down: the 120-day low of 219.10 printed 2026-10-01, the pullback since held a higher low at 232.97, and the 241.36 50-day plus the 245.185 high of 10-05 form one overhead shelf that a Q3 print on better pricing is the natural thing to clear.
recommendations.key_risk: The entry sits above the market and only triggers on strength, so the real risk is not a wrong level but a wrong regime: steel is a cyclical levered to industrial demand, and the macro read elsewhere in this run is hostile to cyclicals — IWM is 8.6% off its high and below its 50-day, XLI is 10.06% off its high, and the bank complex is in correction on fear of additional Fed hikes. If higher-for-longer breaks industrial demand, a pricing-driven beat will be sold rather than bought. Entering before a 10-19 print also means an earnings gap is live, which is why the plan trims half into it instead of holding through. watchlist.demotion_reason: Its own positioning evidence reads against the direction, and the Oct 8 FT report on OpenAI's revenue contradicts the deferral-not-impairment mechanism the thesis rests on.
watchlist.note: RED TEAM CUT (was rank 4, conviction 3, 1.5%). Three reasons, compounding. (1) One of the three evidence kinds holding conviction 3 argues AGAINST the trade in its own words — revision direction flat at 46.9% bullish with a strong-sell outstanding, the weakest sell-side support of any bank checked, and underperformance versus SPY on every window (1m -12.2%, 3m -14.4%) and versus XLF by 8-12 points. An evidence kind that contradicts the direction is not a confirmation, so the score rests on two legs, one of which is the beat record. (2) The load-bearing mechanism is falsified by fresher news the report never saw. The thesis is that the drawdown has a specific reversible cause — ECM fees deferred into 2027 by the OpenAI IPO delay, 'a deferral of revenue, not a loss of it'. But the IPO-delay story broke 2026-06-26 (GS -4.8%, MS -4.1% that day), three and a half months before the September-October drawdown it is being used to explain; and on 2026-10-08, the day before the close this report prices off, the FT reported OpenAI now tells investors annualised revenue is approaching $50bn against the roughly $70bn previously indicated. A mega-listing whose issuer's revenue is ~29% below what investors were told is a repriced fee pool, not a timing problem, and that is an impairment of the exact line the thesis says is only deferred. (3) Correlation: the report concedes GS and MS are one bet and that MS is the stronger by its own discriminator, and notes.md recorded the decision to publish ONE bank idea because XLF BUY already sits in awaiting-entry on this same driver. Keeping the weaker half of an acknowledged single bet as a third expression of one driver is the cluster the correlation test exists to break. Levels and structure were fine (stop 857 below the 868.52 120-day low, R:R 2.09, stop 2.52 ATR); this is a thesis and concentration cut, not an arithmetic one.
watchlist.trigger: Revisit if the post-print reaction holds above the 924.42 20-day on evidence the Q3 fee line is intact independent of the OpenAI calendar, or if revision direction turns positive. Not before MS resolves — it is the same bet.
